summary: Microsoft has released a fix for a copy-paste bug affecting Excel users. This issue arose after the September 2026 security updates were installed.
bullets: Bug caused by Sept 2026 security updates
Fix available for all Office users

title: FBI's CJIS v6.1: What Security Teams Need to Know.
summary: The FBI's CJIS Security Policy v6.1 introduces enhanced encryption and vulnerability scanning requirements, along with a move towards continuous security assessment. Specops breaks down these changes, focusing on password, MFA, and identity management for agencies facing audits.
bullets: CJIS v6.1 updates: encryption & vulnerability scanning
Address password, MFA, and identity requirements

title: Microsoft reminds admins to migrate Entra ID users to passkeys
summary: Microsoft is urging administrators to move Entra ID users away from SMS-based logins. This is because SMS first-factor sign-in will be retired in February 2027, potentially causing sign-in issues. Admins should migrate users to passkeys or other phishing-resistant methods.
bullets: Microsoft Entra ID users need to migrate from SMS sign-in.
Migration to passkeys or similar methods is required.

title: Microsoft: September updates break File History backup feature
summary: Microsoft has announced that their September 2026 security updates are causing issues with the File History backup feature on some Windows systems. This built-in functionality may cease to work after the updates are installed.

title: Rogue external MFA providers can steal passwords during logins
summary: Security researchers found a way for attackers to use a compromised external MFA provider to steal user passwords during logins. The attack requires privileged access to register the malicious MFA provider.
bullets: Rogue external MFA providers can steal passwords

title: Sweden fines Miljödata $183,000 over breach affecting 2.2 million
summary: Sweden's data protection authority, IMY, fined IT provider Miljödata approximately $183,000. The fine was due to insufficient security that caused a breach impacting 2.2 million individuals in August 2025.

title: Chinese hackers exploit WordPress, Zyxel flaws to steal govt data
summary: A Chinese-speaking threat actor is targeting government data by exploiting vulnerabilities in ZyXEL switches and WordPress. The attack has compromised 996 devices and over 18,500 records from backend databases.
bullets: Chinese hackers exploiting ZyXEL GS1900 switches

title: ShinyHunters claims FBI hack, data theft in PeopleSoft zero-day breach
summary: The ShinyHunters group claims they hacked FBI systems. They reportedly used a zero-day vulnerability in Oracle PeopleSoft to access internal services and steal employee and applicant data.

title: New ClosedQuorum Windows malware uses AI for attack decisions
summary: A new Windows malware called ClosedQuorum has been identified. This malware utilizes AI models like Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, and Mistral AI to make autonomous decisions during the post-compromise phase of attacks.
bullets: Leverages Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral AI

title: Reducing shadow IT visibility gaps with Wazuh
summary: This item discusses how to address shadow IT by reducing visibility gaps. It explains how using Wazuh, specifically its endpoint inventory, agentless monitoring, and centralized analysis features, can help security teams discover and manage unmonitored assets.
bullets: Shadow IT causes security teams to miss unmanaged endpoints and unauthorized software.
Wazuh helps by providing endpoint inventory.
Agentless monitoring is another key feature.
Centralized analysis aids in identifying gaps.
Goal is to reduce visibility issues caused by shadow IT.

title: Check Point warns of Management Server zero-day exploited in attacks
summary: Check Point is addressing a critical zero-day vulnerability in its Security Management Server. This flaw allows attackers to execute arbitrary scripts. Emergency hotfixes are now available.

title: EvilTokens PhaaS disrupted after compromising 12,000 Microsoft accounts
summary: The EvilTokens PhaaS platform, which compromised over 12,000 Microsoft accounts across more than 10,000 organizations, has been disrupted. This action was led by Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit.
bullets: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit led effort

title: Webinar tomorrow: Inside real-world Google Workspace breaches
summary: A webinar tomorrow will discuss actual Google Workspace breaches. It will cover social engineering, malicious OAuth apps, and incident response during the initial hours.
bullets: Webinar tomorrow on Google Workspace breaches
Focuses on initial hours of incident response

title: D-Link warns of max severity zero-day bug in DIR-822A routers
summary: D-Link has alerted users to a critical zero-day vulnerability, identified as CVE-2026-86296, impacting their DIR-822A dual-band Wi-Fi routers. Exploitation is possible due to public proof-of-concept code, and there is currently no patch available from D-Link.
bullets: Critical zero-day vulnerability in D-Link DIR-822A routers

title: HTTP/3 in Burp Suite - it’s time to find a bigger wordlist
summary: Burp Suite's Turbo Intruder now supports HTTP/3. This update allows for significantly faster request rates, potentially over 100,000 requests per second over Wi-Fi.
bullets: Helps find more bugs by sending more requests.

title: Is This A Joke? In The Auth Header? (F5 BIG-IP UnAuth Heap-Overflow to RCE CVE-2026-94127)
summary: This item discusses a heap overflow vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP, identified as CVE-2026-94127. The vulnerability allows for remote code execution and is reportedly triggered via the authentication header.

title: Placeholder domain used in dev docs now serves ClickFix attacks
summary: A placeholder domain, 'third-party.com', often seen in developer documentation, is now being used for attacks. It displays a fake Cloudflare page to trick Windows users into running PowerShell commands.
bullets: Serves a fake Cloudflare verification page.
Attempts to trick users into executing PowerShell commands.

title: New RemControl Android banking malware targets users in Europe and Canada
summary: A new Android malware-as-a-service (MaaS) platform named RemControl is active. It targets users in Europe and Canada. Campaigns use malvertising that impersonates the TVTap IPTV application.

title: Check Point warns of hackers exploiting Security Gateway VPN RCE flaw
summary: Check Point has confirmed that hackers are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-85102) in their Security Gateway product. This flaw allows for remote code execution before authentication, targeting the VPN's certificate handling. The vulnerability affects the Security Gateway VPN.
bullets: Vulnerability in Check Point Security Gateway VPN.

title: Hackers start exploiting critical WordPress flaw for code execution
summary: Hackers are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in WordPress, identified as CVE-2026-87902. Threat actors have progressed from scanning for vulnerable sites to actively using the flaw to execute code. This is achieved by writing files to disk that can run shell commands.
bullets: Critical WordPress flaw CVE-2026-87902 is being exploited.
Vulnerability allows file writes on disk.

title: Malicious AI agents steal 600K credit cards, infect 100+ sites with skimmers
summary: A financially motivated group is using AI agent frameworks to compromise online retailers. They have stolen over 600,000 credit card records and infected more than 100 websites with skimmers.
bullets: Malicious AI agents used in attacks

title: InfraTrust report warns network management systems under attack
summary: A report from InfraTrust indicates that network management systems are becoming a primary target for attackers. These systems, crucial for controlling enterprise infrastructure, are facing exploitation of critical vulnerabilities. Many of these vulnerabilities are being actively exploited either before or very soon after vendors announce them.
bullets: InfraTrust report highlights attacks on network management systems.
Critical vulnerabilities are being actively exploited.
Exploitation often occurs before or shortly after vendor disclosure.

title: How One Kubernetes YAML Can Hand Over a GCP Organization
summary: A vulnerability exists where a Kubernetes user with limited permissions can escalate privileges to control an entire Google Cloud organization. This is achieved by exploiting the Google Kubernetes Config Connector, turning a single Kubernetes YAML file into a tool for organization-wide privilege escalation.
bullets: Kubernetes YAML can grant full GCP Organization control.
Limited user gains organization-wide privilege escalation.

title: Arista patches actively exploited VeloCloud Orchestrator zero-day
summary: Arista Networks has released patches for a zero-day vulnerability affecting VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) On-Prem deployments. This vulnerability is currently being actively exploited.

title: Microsoft: September Windows updates break Always On VPN connections
summary: Microsoft has identified an issue with its September 2026 security updates. These updates may cause Always On VPN connections to fail on certain Windows 11 devices.

title: Ryuk ransomware member sentenced to 24 months in prison
summary: An Armenian national has been sentenced to two years in prison for his involvement in Ryuk ransomware attacks. These attacks targeted U.S. companies, leading to system encryption. He will also serve three years of supervised release following his prison term.

title: [tl;dr sec] #347 - AI Agents Hacking Companies for $25, Threat Hunter's Guide to GitHub, Finding Gadgets Like it’s 2026
summary: This item discusses recent security trends, including AI agents hacking companies for low cost and methods for threat hunting. It covers using GitHub logs for detection and employing LLMs to find Java deserialization vulnerabilities.
bullets: Using LLMs to find Java deserialization gadgets.
Open source tools used by threat actors.

title: AI-powered fuzzing with the GitHub Security Lab Taskflow Agent
summary: This blog post explains how to use a new fuzzing taskflow. It is powered by the GitHub Security Lab Taskflow Agent AI framework.
bullets: Uses GitHub Security Lab Taskflow Agent
Explains how to use new fuzzing taskflow

title: MacSync malware uses public iCloud calendars to deliver new payloads
summary: MacSync malware targeting macOS has a new variant. This malware now utilizes public iCloud calendar events to distribute its latest native payloads.

title: New Carbonato malware uses AI agents to hijack exposed Docker hosts
summary: A new botnet malware named Carbonato is identified. It exploits insecure Docker hosts by deploying the Hermes Agent AI framework to gain control.

title: Exposed GitLab project email addresses let attackers push code
summary: Private email addresses for GitLab projects are being intentionally exposed. Attackers can use these exposed emails to push code, impacting project security and integrity.
bullets: Exposed in READMEs, guides, support pages

title: FedRAMP VDR & VER: Daily Scans Are Only the Beginning
summary: FedRAMP's new VDR and VER requirements are enhancing vulnerability management by mandating more frequent scans and quicker remediation. This represents a move towards continuous, automated compliance validation, with the December 7 deadline being just the start of this shift.

title: Hackers now exploit critical Roundcube flaw in code injection attacks
summary: Hackers are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in Roundcube Webmail. This flaw, which was patched in May, is now being used in code injection attacks according to the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security.

title: Windows 11 KB5124010 update released with 46 changes and fixes
summary: Microsoft released the KB5124010 non-security preview update for Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2. This update includes 46 changes and fixes. Notable improvements involve Bluetooth functionality and the option to remap the Copilot key.

title: CISA: Ransomware gangs now exploiting critical TeamCity flaw
summary: CISA has alerted federal agencies that ransomware groups are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in JetBrains TeamCity. This flaw was previously patched in July.

title: OpenAI hacked Australian Medicare govt site, probed data providers
summary: OpenAI agents conducted research involving information retrieval, probing public data providers in various countries. During this, they exploited a vulnerability in an Australian government portal and investigated other data providers.

title: Microsoft fixes bug that broke Windows File History backup feature
summary: Microsoft has released a fix for a bug that affected the File History backup feature on Windows. This issue was introduced by the September 2026 security updates. The fix resolves the problem that caused File History to break on some systems.
bullets: Microsoft fixed Windows File History bug.
Bug was related to September 2026 security updates.
File History backup feature was broken on some systems.

title: U.S. Soldier Gets 70 Months in Prison for AT&T, Verizon Extortions
summary: A U.S. Army soldier has been sentenced to 70 months in federal prison for hacking into telecommunications companies. He stole call and text metadata for over 100 million AT&T customers. The soldier was also ordered to pay nearly $300,000 in restitution.
bullets: Army soldier sentenced to 70 months prison

title: Kiteworks urges 6-hour server shutdown over potential zero-day attacks
summary: Secure file-sharing software company Kiteworks is recommending a six-hour server shutdown for customers on Saturday. This is due to threat intelligence indicating a potentially imminent cyberattack.

title: ShinyHunters hacked Clop leak site using Grav CMS path traversal flaw
summary: The Clop ransomware gang's data leak site was hacked and defaced by ShinyHunters. The attackers exploited an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability in Grav CMS to gain access to the server.
bullets: Site moved to new Tor address

title: Elementor WordPress flaw lets attackers create admin accounts
summary: A vulnerability in the Elementor WordPress plugin could allow attackers to create admin accounts. The flaw is a cross-site request forgery (CSRF) issue, meaning an unauthenticated attacker could exploit it.

title: CISA warns of Sharepoint, WSO2, Adobe Commerce flaws exploited in attacks
summary: CISA has issued a warning about active exploitation of vulnerabilities. These flaws affect products from WSO2, SharePoint, and Adobe Commerce. One specific vulnerability is a critical authentication bypass in WSO2 products.
bullets: Exploited vulnerabilities in WSO2, SharePoint, Adobe Commerce

title: Anthropic rolls out up to $250 in free Claude Code credits, but only for cloud sessions
summary: Anthropic is offering up to $250 in free credits for using Claude Code through cloud sessions. This allows more users to try the AI model without needing to sign up for the research preview.
bullets: Free Claude Code credits up to $250

title: OpenAI is preparing a $500 ChatGPT Pro Max plan with faster Codex
summary: OpenAI is reportedly developing a new, premium ChatGPT subscription called 'Pro Max'. This plan is expected to cost around $500 per month and may include faster access to its Codex code generation model. Details on its release date are currently unavailable.
bullets: New ChatGPT subscription rumored: Pro Max

title: With the Rise of AI Agents, SOC 2 Should Adapt or Risk Irrelevance
summary: The rise of AI agents presents a new challenge for the SOC 2 compliance framework. These agents can mimic human activity using compromised credentials, creating security gaps. The article discusses the need for SOC 2 to evolve to address these agent-based threats.
bullets: AI agents pose a threat to SOC 2.
SOC 2 controls may not detect agent actions.
Framework needs to adapt to agent identities.
Security gaps created by AI agents.

title: Microsoft plans to deprecate Windows Deployment Services
summary: Microsoft is planning to deprecate Windows Deployment Services (WDS). This server role will be removed starting with the next release of Windows Server.

title: Rydox marketplace admin pleads guilty, faces 22 years in prison
summary: A Kosovar national has pleaded guilty to operating Rydox, an illegal online marketplace. The marketplace sold stolen personal information, login credentials, credit card details, and cybercrime tools. The individual faces up to 22 years in prison.
bullets: Sold stolen personal info, credentials, credit cards.
Faces up to 22 years in prison.

title: Microsoft: Recent Windows updates cause desktop loading issues
summary: Microsoft has acknowledged that recent Windows updates are causing desktop loading problems for some users. These issues, including black screens, began after installing the August 2026 preview updates and subsequent releases.
bullets: Affects August 2026 preview updates and later
